Lessons9 lessons
1. Introduction to CBT▾

Understand links among situations, thoughts, emotions, body sensations, and actions.

2. Thinking Traps▾

Identify common patterns such as catastrophizing, filtering, mind-reading, and all-or-nothing thinking.

3. Thought Records▾

Use a structured record to examine evidence and develop a balanced thought.

4. Understanding Worry▾

Distinguish worry from problem solving and notice beliefs that keep worry going.

5. Safety Behaviours and Exposure▾

Identify avoidance and safety behaviours that maintain anxiety.

6. Challenging Negative Thoughts▾

Question an unhelpful thought with evidence, alternatives, and a more balanced view.

7. Worry Time▾

Set a deliberate time for worry so it takes up less of the day.

8. Box Breathing, Gratitude, and Positive Self-Talk▾

Practise brief calming and reflection tools that can support wider skills work.

9. Five Factor Model and Worry Tree▾

Map a problem across five factors and decide whether action or acceptance fits.
